module_title: The Human Eye, Vision Defects, and Atmospheric Phenomena
introduction: The human eye is a natural optical instrument. Understanding its defects and how to correct them is mandatory for all competitive exams. This level also covers the physics behind rainbows and the blue sky.

core_concepts.title: Anatomy of the Eye
core_concepts.description:
1. Cornea: The outer clear window where most refraction occurs. 
2. Iris & Pupil: Controls the amount of light entering. 
3. Retina: The screen where the 'Real and Inverted' image is formed. 
4. Ciliary Muscles: Change the focal length of the eye lens (Accommodation).

core_concepts.title: Defects of Vision and Corrections
core_concepts.description:
1. Myopia (Near-sightedness): Can see near, cannot see far. Image forms 'in front' of the retina. Correction: Concave Lens (Diverging). 
2. Hypermetropia (Far-sightedness): Can see far, cannot see near. Image forms 'behind' the retina. Correction: Convex Lens (Converging). 
3. Presbyopia: Old age far-sightedness due to weak ciliary muscles. Correction: Bifocal lenses. 
4. Astigmatism: Blurred vision due to irregular cornea curvature. Correction: Cylindrical lenses.

core_concepts.title: Dispersion of Light
core_concepts.description:
The splitting of white light into its 7 component colors (VIBGYOR) when passing through a prism. 
Red bends the LEAST (highest wavelength). Violet bends the MOST (lowest wavelength). 
Example: Formation of a Rainbow (involves Dispersion, Refraction, and TIR).

core_concepts.title: Scattering of Light
core_concepts.description:
When light hits tiny particles in the atmosphere, it scatters in all directions. Shorter wavelengths (Blue) scatter much more than longer wavelengths (Red). 
Examples: The blue color of the sky, the red color of the sun at sunrise/sunset, and danger signals being red.

important_entities.name: Twinkling of Stars
important_entities.significance: Stars twinkle because their light passes through different layers of Earth's atmosphere with varying temperatures and densities, causing the starlight to continuously bend (refract). Planets do NOT twinkle because they are much closer and act as extended light sources.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'Near-sightedness' sounds like you have trouble seeing near. IT IS THE OPPOSITE. The name tells you what you CAN see. Near-sighted (Myopia) = You CAN see near perfectly, but far objects are blurry.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: MYopia requires a conCAVE lens. HYpermetropia requires a conVEX lens.

exam_strategy_tips: NDA/CDS Questions: 'Why are danger signals red?' Answer: Because red light has the longest wavelength and is scattered the least by fog or smoke, making it visible from a long distance.
